data.why: The repository ships complete synthetic EDF recordings (no real patient data) with documented ground-truth manifests specifically for trying out the app; the README's own quick-start workflow is to upload these on the File & Patient page.

goals: Upload a routine EEG/ECG recording and get the channels automatically classified as EEG/ECG/EOG/EMG/vital
Review EEG spectral measures (band power, alpha background rhythm, anterior/posterior gradient, hemispheric asymmetry) and confirm the alpha peak frequency and amplitude asymmetry match expectations
Screen the recording for suspected atrial fibrillation and ectopy upstream of HRV analysis, and interpret graded-certainty flags rather than a diagnosis
Compute heart-rate variability (time domain, frequency domain, DFA, Poincaré) over a sufficiently long stationary segment and compare total vs artifact-corrected results
Fit the aperiodic (1/f) component of the EEG spectrum and compare the app's own log-log fit against the FOOOF/specparam reference implementation
Export a provenance-tagged PDF/Excel report (version, commit, package versions, recording hash) so two analyses of the same recording can be compared later

review.summary: The tree is a faithful, well-structured account of the README's stated workflow, and every one of the ten screens I opened shows what its node claims. It needs a check re-run with the password and a few additions before filing: the AF fixture, the method-evidence list, complexity measures and the visual report.
